This offers a model for relative mandibular prognathism from maxillary underdevelopment; the same growth-plate process has not been demonstrated in affected humans.

evidence.snippet: aortic root dilation, and multiple visceral and peripheral arterial aneurysms at the age of 54 years
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:29625025; one biallelic patient demonstrates vascular disease beyond the thoracic aorta.

evidence.snippet: thoracic computed tomography (CT) revealed aortic dissection in the descending aorta (DeBakey type III).
evidence.explanation: Direct vascular diagnosis in a compound heterozygous patient.

steps/9.description: Biallelic LTBP3 variants predispose some affected individuals to aortic and other arterial aneurysms and dissection. The molecular mechanism remains unresolved: altered latent TGF-beta handling and matrix functions are candidates. Mouse aortic dimensions vary with age, genetic background and normalization, and protection from rupture in a fibrillin-deficient double mutant does not establish benefit from reducing LTBP3 in patients.

evidence.snippet: The almost complete absence of enamel in both primary and permanent dentitions (Fig. 1A and B) led to the diagnosis of hypoplastic AI, thereby explaining the yellow, small and spaced appearance of the teeth.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the enamel phenotype in both dentitions and its clinical appearance.

evidence.snippet: The 2 patients from the first family had dental anomalies and short stature syndrome, brachyolmia and nephrocalcinosis with difference in severity
evidence.explanation: Independent replication in a different population, and a reminder that severity varies within a family carrying the same allele.

steps/10.description: Enamel is thin to almost absent in primary and permanent dentitions, often producing small, yellow and spaced teeth. Dentin was normal in one studied family, but abnormalities have been reported in another.

evidence.snippet: The spine radiographs show platyspondyly with indentations of both upper and lower vertebral endplates.
evidence.explanation: Direct radiographic documentation in an affected individual.

evidence.snippet: the proband showed short stature, short trunk, scoliosis with accentuated lordosis, facial dysmorphisms, pterygium colli, varus knees, lower limbs diplegia and platyspondyly
evidence.explanation: Independent documentation of platyspondyly with the associated short-trunk habitus.

steps/11.description: Generalized vertebral-body flattening and endplate indentation are characteristic. Mild long-bone and hand abnormalities can coexist.

evidence.snippet: Only 20 individuals from nine families have been previously reported, with a consistent phenotype of short stature, brachyolmia, and amelogenesis imperfecta.
evidence.explanation: Records short stature as one of the three consistent features across the published cohort.

evidence.snippet: with normal limb/torso ratios and proximal/distal limb ratios.
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:19344874 documents proportionate stature in affected family members.

steps/12.description: Often associated with a short trunk, but proportionate short stature has also been reported. Severity varies, including mildly reduced height in some children.

evidence.snippet: Class III mandibular prognathism encountered in family 1 was due to maxillary underdevelopment
evidence.explanation: Attributes the occlusal finding to maxillary underdevelopment, which is the phenotype bound here.

evidence.snippet: Skull radiograph reveals absent pneumatization of sinuses and mandibular prognathism secondary to underdevelopment of the maxilla.
evidence.explanation: Radiographic confirmation, with the additional finding of absent sinus pneumatisation in the same underdeveloped maxilla.

steps/13.description: Maxillary underdevelopment accounts for relative mandibular prognathism in the 2015 family and has a corresponding upper-jaw phenotype in knockout mice.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with compound heterozygous or homozygous variants in these families have aneurysms and dissections of the thoracic aorta
evidence.explanation: Primary 2018 family study.

steps/14.description: Thoracic aortic aneurysms have been reported in biallelic LTBP3 families. Age of presentation and affected aortic segments vary; dissection can occur in adulthood.

evidence.snippet: thoracic computed tomography (CT) revealed aortic dissection in the descending aorta (DeBakey type III).
evidence.explanation: Primary report of a compound heterozygous patient.

steps/15.description: Type A and type B dissections have occurred in adults with biallelic LTBP3 disease. The 2021 Chinese patient had type B dissection at age 42.

evidence.snippet: abdominal aortic aneurysm requiring surgical repair at the age of 44
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:29625025, family TAA909 proband.

steps/16.description: Abdominal aneurysm requiring repair at age 44 was reported in a compound heterozygous patient, followed by visceral and peripheral arterial aneurysms.

evidence.snippet: Echocardiography revealed aortic root dilatation (diameter: 38 mm, z-score: þ 4.59), mitral valve prolapse
evidence.explanation: Direct examination of the 24-year-old sibling in the full report; the paper describes root dilatation and prolapse in all three siblings. The cached PDF preserves the plus sign as þ.

steps/17.description: Root enlargement was present in all three siblings reported in 2025, including an asymptomatic eight-year-old. Thoracoabdominal CT found no additional aneurysm, rupture or dissection. The ontology term includes aortic root dilatation as a synonym.

evidence.snippet: She suffered of repeated dental abscesses, leading to the extraction of several teeth at ages 2½ and 5 years.
evidence.explanation: Direct observation in the cited study; frequency across affected individuals is not established.

steps/18.description: Recurrent dental abscesses can occur in childhood and lead to extraction of severely affected teeth.

evidence.snippet: arterial aneurysms (innominate, common carotid; 58)
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:29625025, primary clinical table; innominate denotes the brachiocephalic artery.

steps/19.description: Reported at age 58 in the biallelic woman from family TAA376, alongside aortic disease and cervical arterial tortuosity.

evidence.snippet: arterial aneurysms (innominate, common carotid; 58)
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:29625025, primary clinical table; innominate denotes the brachiocephalic artery.

steps/20.description: Reported at age 58 in the biallelic woman from family TAA376, alongside aortic disease and cervical arterial tortuosity.

edges/1.description: Loss of intact LTBP3 can impair latent-complex assembly; individual variant effects are often predicted.

edges/2.description: Biallelic variants are associated with aneurysm and dissection, but the intervening molecular steps remain unresolved.

evidence.snippet: the synchondroses in the skull base were obliterated within 2 weeks of birth.
evidence.explanation: Null-mouse histology, not a human observation.

edges/3.description: Ltbp3 loss causes premature cranial-base ossification in null mice; applicability to human disease remains inferred.

edges/4.description: Abnormal complexes may alter matrix incorporation and subsequent ligand availability.

edges/5.description: Matrix incorporation controls latent ligand localization and activation.

edges/6.description: A proposed link between altered ligand availability and enamel-organ dysfunction; patient signaling measurements are lacking.

edges/7.description: The vertebral mechanism is inferred from expression and pathway biology, not demonstrated by a model reproducing platyspondyly.

edges/8.description: Enamel-organ dysfunction produces reduced and disorganized enamel.

edges/9.description: Clinical manifestation of deficient enamel.

edges/10.description: Loss of protective dental tissue can contribute to recurrent infection.

edges/11.description: Vertebral body flattening is a characteristic clinical endpoint.

edges/12.description: Short stature can be disproportionate or proportionate; contributions outside the vertebrae vary.

edges/13.description: Premature cranial-base growth arrest can shorten the upper jaw in the mouse model.

edges/14.description: Aneurysmal disease can affect thoracic segments.

edges/16.description: Arterial wall failure can produce dissection.

edges/17.description: Root enlargement may be detected before other aortic complications.

edges/18.description: Non-aortic arterial involvement demonstrates systemic vascular disease.

edges/19.description: Non-aortic arterial involvement demonstrates systemic vascular disease.

evidence.snippet: we identified the LTBP3 (latent TGF-beta binding protein 3) gene as the underlying causal gene responsible for this rare autosomal recessive disorder
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease assertion from the defining study.

evidence.snippet: We identified two novel LTBP3 homozygous variants, the c.2495delT deletion (p.Phe832SerfsTer36) and the c.3716 G>A (p.Cys1239Tyr) missense variant, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Extends the allelic spectrum to include a missense allele in a previously unreported population.

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel and common LTBP3 gene pathogenic variant responsible for short stature, brachyolmia and amelogenesis imperfecta in Druze Arab patients.
evidence.explanation: A founder allele in a defined community, which is the one context in this disease where carrier screening rather than case-by-case exome sequencing becomes the sensible strategy.

evidence.snippet: One homozygote region in chromosome 11 (11p11.2- 11q13.3) was found in all patients.
evidence.explanation: The homozygosity-mapping result that localised the gene in these families, and the evidence that the allele is shared by descent rather than recurrent.

evidence.snippet: The proband's father, who carried the heterozygous variant c.3107-2A > G had short stature and prognathic mandible.
evidence.explanation: The compound heterozygous proband and heterozygous parents had features in this family; his heterozygous brother was unaffected.

genes/0.notes: Biallelic LTBP3 loss-of-function variants cause DASS. Transcript studies support allele-dependent effects, while most protein consequences remain inferred. Monoallelic acromicric and geleophysic dysplasias are distinct allelic conditions; acromicric dysplasia may include dental abnormalities. Heterozygous relatives in some DASS pedigrees have variable features, so carrier findings require variant- and family-specific interpretation.

evidence.snippet: Consequently, dental pulps were affected; thus, root canal treatments and pulpotomies were performed. In addition, the posterior teeth were crowned to preserve the remaining teeth structures and maintain the occlusion.
evidence.explanation: Direct treatment report in the affected siblings of family B.

evidence.snippet: In young patients with AI symptoms of pain and hypersensitivity decreased, and aesthetics were improved following all types of restorative therapy
evidence.explanation: The outcome that justifies early restoration - symptom relief, not only appearance. INDIRECT because the review covers non-syndromic AI in under-19s rather than LTBP3-related disease.

evidence.snippet: single-tooth ceramic crowns should be the first choice of treatment
evidence.explanation: A specific first-line recommendation from a 2017-2023 review of 38 eligible studies. INDIRECT for the same reason.

treatments/0.description: Protect affected teeth and restore function using individualized dental rehabilitation. The 2024 DASS series reports root canal treatment, pulpotomies and posterior crowns. Broader AI evidence supports reduced pain and hypersensitivity after restoration, but comparative effectiveness and durability specific to LTBP3 remain unestablished.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Replaces the missing protective layer. It does not act on amelogenesis, which has already failed by the time teeth erupt.

evidence.snippet: Orthodontic treatment and orthognathic surgery were performed as part of the prosthetic treatment plan to achieve acceptable and durable results.
evidence.explanation: Describes the combined approach. INDIRECT: a single case of non-syndromic hypocalcified AI, cited for the management pattern rather than for a genotype-matched outcome.

evidence.snippet: No deterioration in the rehabilitation was found after 5 years of follow-up.
evidence.explanation: The durability result, which is the reason to prefer a staged multidisciplinary plan over repeated restoration. INDIRECT for the same reason.

treatments/1.description: Orthodontic and orthognathic procedures may address malocclusion and jaw disproportion. The cited five-year treatment result is from nonsyndromic hypocalcified AI with a class II relationship, whereas an LTBP3 family had class III malocclusion from maxillary hypoplasia; the same operative plan cannot be presumed appropriate.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Orthognathic procedures can address jaw disproportion; evidence here is extrapolated from nonsyndromic AI.

evidence.snippet: They are followed up annually at cardiology clinics with detailed medical history, physical examinations, ECG, and echocardiography.
evidence.explanation: Directly reported DASS follow-up; intervals were adjusted for progression.

evidence.snippet: The decision regarding the need for surgery was made based on close (6-month) follow-up of the aortic root expansion rate.
evidence.explanation: Monitoring strategy in the reported family; surgery itself was not reported.

treatments/2.description: The 2025 DASS series reports cardiology follow-up with history, examination, ECG and echocardiography, plus thoracoabdominal CT to assess additional aortic disease. Six-month assessment of root expansion informed surgical decisions in that family. The schedule is reported care, not a validated universal surveillance interval.

evidence.snippet: She suffered of repeated dental abscesses, leading to the extraction of several teeth at ages 2½ and 5 years.
evidence.explanation: Direct observation in the cited study; frequency across affected individuals is not established.

treatments/3.description: Extractions were reported for recurrent abscesses in young affected children; selection depends on dental infection, restorability and dentition.

evidence.snippet: The oldest girl underwent surgery for an S-shaped scoliosis.
evidence.explanation: Direct observation in the cited study; frequency across affected individuals is not established.

treatments/4.description: Surgery for severe S-shaped scoliosis was reported in an affected girl; the study does not establish a uniform operative indication.

evidence.snippet: TEVAR surgery was then performed.
evidence.explanation: Actual intervention following type B dissection.

evidence.snippet: abdominal aortic aneurysm requiring surgical repair at the age of 44
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:29625025.

treatments/5.description: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed for type B dissection in the 2021 patient; abdominal aneurysm repair was reported in a 2018 patient. Procedure and timing require assessment of the specific vascular lesion.

evidence.snippet: monitoring for mitral valve prolapse-related arrhythmias was undertaken, requiring beta-blocker treatment during follow-up.
evidence.explanation: Directly reported treatment in the 2025 family.

treatments/6.description: Beta-blocker treatment was reported during follow-up of patients 1 and 3 in the 2025 series for mitral-prolapse-related arrhythmias. The agent, dose and comparative efficacy were not specified; this is not evidence of correction of LTBP3 disease.

evidence.snippet: After segregation analysis of affected siblings and parents was completed, genetic counselling was given to the family. It was explained that there was a 25% risk of recurrence in each pregnancy.
evidence.explanation: The reported parents were carriers; this probability is conditional on that parental genotype.

treatments/7.description: Confirm segregation and provide recurrence counseling. When both parents carry a pathogenic allele, each pregnancy has a 25% probability of biallelic inheritance. A reported de novo allele illustrates why this calculation must follow family testing.

hypotheses/0.description: LTBP3 loss alters the extracellular handling of latent TGF-beta and is associated with dental, skeletal and vascular disease. Biochemical studies establish latent-complex binding and matrix incorporation. Reduced local TGF-beta signaling is proposed for parts of the dental and skeletal phenotype, but has not been directly demonstrated for all patient alleles or tissues. Vascular signaling responses vary by model and disease stage, and TGF-beta-independent matrix functions remain possible.

evidence.snippet: Platyspondyly however was not observed in the Ltbp3−/− knockout mice.
evidence.explanation: Directly reported failure to reproduce the human axial phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Increased bone density was present in the spine and at the base of the skull.
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:19344874; radiographs and quantitative assessment were reported.

open_questions/0.rationale: The null mouse reproduces enamel and maxillary abnormalities but not vertebral flattening. Human bone density varies, so density does not supply a universal opposite-direction mismatch. Allele-specific residual function, developmental timing, biomechanics and functions beyond TGF-beta regulation remain plausible explanations.

evidence.snippet: enlargement of the ventricle and OFT in DKO animals precedes hyperactivation of TGFβ signaling and not vice versa.
evidence.explanation: The double-knockout zebrafish result limits a uniform primary signaling-direction claim.

evidence.snippet: we found that ATA diameter is slightly greater than normal in Ltbp3−/− mice, but not significantly so, at least at the ages studied.
evidence.explanation: Independent allometric analysis limits the strength of the mouse-to-human aortopathy correspondence.

open_questions/1.rationale: Human genetic evidence for aortopathy is strong, but mouse results differ with body-size normalization and Fbn1 background. In dual-paralog zebrafish mutants, elevated pSmad3 follows dilation. These observations do not establish a uniform primary increase or decrease in signaling or justify extrapolating a signaling-directed therapy to DASS.

evidence.snippet: the hearing impairment phenotype in Egyptian patients of family A has a separate transmission mechanism independent of LTBP3.
evidence.explanation: Authors’ attribution; this statement does not independently establish CABP2 variant pathogenicity.

evidence.snippet: The mother and brother of the proband carried the heterozygous variant p.Arg545ProfsTer22, but only the mother showed any DASS characteristics.
evidence.explanation: Variable findings among heterozygous relatives argue against uniform carrier penetrance.

open_questions/2.rationale: The 2021 boy had neurological findings and additional TPH1 and EDA variants of uncertain relevance. The 2024 authors attributed hearing impairment in one family to a separate CABP2 mechanism, although their pathogenicity interpretation is not definitive. The 2022 abstract lists tricuspid prolapse and abnormal dentin across a family without resolving every finding by genotype. These observations should not automatically become established biallelic LTBP3 manifestations.

evidence.snippet: In families 4 and 5, which are reportedly not related but reside in adjacent villages, we identified a homozygous missense variant in GATC: c.233T>G; p.Met78Arg.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the causal allele.

evidence.snippet: Due to their essential role in protein synthesis, residual enzyme activity characterizes disorders of tRNA synthetases, and complete loss-of-function is thought to be embryonically lethal
evidence.explanation: The reasoning behind curating this as a partial rather than complete loss of function.

evidence.snippet: we observed a possible relation between clinical severity and the degree of amino acid conservation
evidence.explanation: The proposed genotype-severity relationship, in the authors' own hedged terms.

steps/1.description: The initiating lesion is the homozygous GATC missense allele c.233T>G (p.Met78Arg), the only GATC variant reported in this disorder. That it is a missense rather than a null allele is not incidental. Complete loss of a tRNA-charging function is thought to be embryonically lethal, so a viable patient must retain some residual activity; every patient in the defining series carried at least one missense allele. The authors go further and propose that severity tracks the degree of conservation of the affected residue - the prenatal-onset GATB and QRSL1 families had variants at highly conserved residues, while the infantile-onset GATC families had a variant at a moderately conserved one. On that reading the later onset of COXPD42 relative to its GatCAB siblings is a consequence of a milder residual activity, not of the subunit affected.

evidence.snippet: In subject P4B with mutations in GATC, the steady state level of GatC in fibroblasts was decreased to 20% of controls (Fig. 3e), and the GatA and GatB protein levels were equally substantially decreased (Fig. 3e), probably due to the instability of the individual subunits when they are not incorporated in the GatCAB trimer.
evidence.explanation: The central observation: a GATC variant depletes all three subunits, with the authors' own hedged explanation.

evidence.snippet: we analyzed their mRNA levels in exponentially growing fibroblasts from patients P3A and P4B and found no significant changes in the transcriptional rate of the three genes compared to controls
evidence.explanation: Excludes a transcriptional explanation and localises the effect to protein stability.

evidence.snippet: In the bacterial GatCAB complex, GatA and GatB possess the catalytic amidase and kinase functions, respectively, while GatC serves as a stabilizing linker between them.
evidence.explanation: Establishes GatC's structural rather than catalytic role, which is what makes trimer destabilization the mechanism.

steps/2.description:
In the bacterial complex GatA carries the amidase function and GatB the kinase function, while GatC serves as a stabilizing linker between them. The patient data show that this architectural role is what fails. In GATC patient fibroblasts GatC protein falls to about 20 percent of control, and GatA and GatB fall by a comparable amount - even though neither of their genes is mutated. The likely explanation is that the individual subunits are unstable when not incorporated into the trimer.
Crucially this is post-transcriptional: mRNA levels of QRSL1, GATB and GATC were unchanged in patient fibroblasts, so the loss of GatA and GatB is protein instability rather than a transcriptional response. A GATC lesion therefore behaves as a lesion of the whole amidotransferase, which is why a subunit with no catalytic activity of its own produces the same disease as the catalytic subunits.

evidence.snippet: mt-tRNAGln is indirectly charged by a transamidation reaction involving the GatCAB aminoacyl-tRNA amidotransferase complex.
evidence.explanation: States the indirect charging pathway this node represents.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, mitochondria are exclusively dependent on the GatCAB complex for appropriate charging of mt-tRNAGln with glutamine.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that no alternative charging route exists, which is why a GatCAB defect cannot be compensated.

evidence.snippet: After 3 days in culture medium without glutamine, fibroblasts from P1A, P3A, and P4B show decreased glutamine charging of mt-tRNAGln compared to control fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the charging defect and its dependence on glutamine withdrawal. P4B is one of the GATC patients, so this is direct evidence for this disorder rather than for a sibling GatCAB defect.

steps/3.description:
Mitochondria have no glutaminyl-tRNA synthetase. Glutaminyl mt-tRNA is therefore charged indirectly in two steps: EARS2 mischarges it with glutamate, and GatCAB transamidates the Glu-mt-tRNA(Gln) to Gln-mt-tRNA(Gln) using free glutamine as amide donor. The same paper closed the obvious escape route - cytoplasmic QARS had been reported in some databases as dual-localised, but QARS-GFP did not co-localise with TOM20, cellular fractionation showed no mitochondrial enrichment, and the trace that did fractionate with mitochondria was proteinase-K sensitive. Mitochondria depend exclusively on GatCAB.
The defect is conditional on substrate supply, which is the single most important practical fact about this disorder. In standard glutamine-rich culture medium patient fibroblasts charge mt-tRNA(Gln) similarly to controls; only after three days without glutamine does charging fall. A normal-looking fibroblast assay run under standard conditions is therefore not evidence against the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: revealed a strong and generalized mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis defect after a 90-min pulse in P4B (GATC) and in P3A (QRSL1) patients' fibroblasts
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement of the translation defect in the GATC patient's cells.

evidence.snippet: However, during continued translation, the rate of charging mt-tRNAGln with glutamine cannot keep up with the demand, and translation efficiency decreases
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the defect is one of charging throughput under sustained demand rather than an absolute block.

evidence.snippet: It is remarkable that this impairment of mitochondrial DNA-encoded protein synthesis correlates with no apparent changes in the steady state levels of representative OXPHOS proteins reflecting the assembled mitochondrial complexes
evidence.explanation: Curated as PARTIAL: the translation defect is real but is not reflected in steady-state subunit levels in fibroblasts, which is a caution against using that readout to exclude the diagnosis.

steps/4.description:
Pulse labelling with radiolabelled methionine in the presence of emetine, to silence cytoplasmic translation, showed a strong and generalized defect in mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis in the GATC patient's fibroblasts. Because glutamine codons occur throughout the thirteen mtDNA-encoded proteins, the defect is general rather than selective for one complex - this is the reason the disease is a combined rather than an isolated respiratory chain deficiency.
A subtlety worth preserving: the reduction in newly synthesized protein was not accompanied by reduced steady-state levels of assembled OXPHOS subunits in fibroblasts. Chloramphenicol chase experiments showed the explanation is increased stability of the existing subunits, which together with residual GatCAB activity masks the defect in that cell type. A chloramphenicol block and release experiment made the kinetics visible: translation resumes at a near-normal rate for a few hours on accumulated charged tRNA, then falls behind as charging fails to keep up with demand.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of the mitochondrial respiratory chain enzymes in all patients showed a combined deficiency with decreased activities of complexes I and IV, and low or borderline-low activity of complex III, that varied between the different tissues tested
evidence.explanation: The defining biochemical finding and its tissue variability.

evidence.snippet: observed subassemblies of complex I were present in heart and muscle (Fig. 4b), and were more prominent in fibroblasts when grown in medium without glutamine

steps/5.description:
All patients showed a combined deficiency with decreased activities of complexes I and IV and low or borderline-low complex III, varying between tissues. The pattern is exactly what a general mitochondrial translation defect predicts: complexes I, III, IV and V contain mtDNA-encoded subunits and are affected, while complex II, which is entirely nuclear-encoded, is not. Incompletely assembled complex I subcomplexes are demonstrable, and are more prominent when glutamine is withdrawn.
Conformance note: this node conforms to the module's central bioenergetic node, but only in part. The module pairs decreased oxidative phosphorylation with increased reactive oxygen species. Decreased oxidative phosphorylation is directly evidenced in these patients; the reactive oxygen species arm is evidenced only in a mouse-cell GatA knockdown, not in GATC patients, and is curated on that model rather than asserted here. The module's upstream node - age-related mitochondrial damage and mtDNA mutation - does not apply to a primary nuclear-gene translation defect, which is why conformance is declared at this node alone.

steps/6.description: The translation defect is not expressed equally across tissues. It is most pronounced in heart, less so in skeletal muscle, and nearly absent in fibroblasts - a gradient that tracks oxidative demand and explains why a cardiomyopathy rather than a multisystem encephalopathy is the presenting disease. Post-mortem cardiac tissue from a GATC patient shows the morphological signature of the compensation attempted: massive mitochondrial proliferation displacing the contractile elements on electron microscopy, and a corresponding increase in mitochondrial mass by SDHB immunostaining.

evidence.snippet: Anemia, which is a rare symptom in mitochondrial disorders11–13, was frequently present, ranging in severity from mild to severe prenatal anemia requiring intrauterine transfusions. The bone marrow biopsy did not show ringed sideroblasts in any of the subjects.

steps/7.description:
The clinical endpoint. All five GATC patients presented between two and 5.5 months with cardiomyopathy and lactic acidosis, and none survived beyond 6.5 months. Anaemia accompanied the presentation in every GATC patient in whom it was assessed, which is notable because anaemia is a rare feature of mitochondrial disease; bone marrow examination showed no ringed sideroblasts. Liver dysfunction and mildly elevated creatine kinase were present in four of the five.
The onset timing separates COXPD42 from its GatCAB siblings: the GATB and QRSL1 families in the same report had prenatal onset with hydrops or growth restriction and died within days, whereas the GATC families presented in infancy.

evidence.explanation: Establishes the subunit-to-gene mapping of the complex.

evidence.snippet: it is first charged with glutamic acid (Glu) by mitochondrial glutamyl-tRNA synthetase (EARS2), after which the Glu-mt-tRNAGln is transamidated into Gln-mt-tRNAGln, using free glutamine as an amide donor
evidence.explanation: Places EARS2 upstream of GatCAB in the same pathway.

genes/0.notes:
GATC encodes GatC, the smallest of the three subunits of the mitochondrial glutamyl-tRNA(Gln) amidotransferase. Unlike GatA (QRSL1) and GatB (GATB), it has no catalytic activity of its own: in the bacterial complex it is the stabilizing linker holding the amidase and kinase subunits together. That architecture is why a GATC lesion is not a milder version of the others but an equivalent one - loss of GatC depletes GatA and GatB too.
Only one pathogenic GATC allele is reported: homozygous c.233T>G (p.Met78Arg), in two families from adjacent villages. The entire clinical description of COXPD42 therefore rests on one variant in five patients, and the allelic and phenotypic range of the disorder is unknown.
GATC sits within a coherent gene group. QRSL1 (GatA) and GATB (GatB) cause the two sibling COXPD entities in the same report; upstream, EARS2 performs the first, mischarging step of the same two-step pathway. A COXPD42-like presentation should prompt sequencing of all three GatCAB genes rather than GATC alone, since they are clinically indistinguishable at presentation.

open_questions/0.rationale:
This is the most obvious therapeutic idea the biology suggests, and it is entirely untested. The observation behind it is robust: patient fibroblasts charge mt-tRNA(Gln) at near-normal levels in glutamine-rich medium and fail only when glutamine is withdrawn, and complex I subassemblies become more prominent under withdrawal. Glutamine is the amide donor for the reaction, so substrate concentration plausibly compensates for reduced enzyme.
Three things stand between that and a treatment, and this entry curates no treatment for exactly these reasons. First, the experiments show that supraphysiological culture glutamine masks the defect - not that physiologically achievable plasma glutamine would. Second, the cells in which the rescue is seen are fibroblasts, the tissue least affected in the disease; the heart is the tissue that must be rescued, and no cardiac model exists. Third, and most limiting, the chloramphenicol block-and-release experiment showed that translation keeps pace only briefly before charging falls behind sustained demand, which suggests the constraint is enzymatic throughput rather than substrate supply once demand is high. A cardiomyocyte never stops translating.

open_questions/1.rationale:
Everything in this entry describes five patients from two families in adjacent villages, all homozygous for the same GATC allele, reported in one paper. That is not a phenotype; it is one genotype observed several times.
The distinction matters because the paper's own severity model predicts a range. It proposes that clinical severity tracks residual GatCAB activity, and that residual activity tracks the conservation of the mutated residue - which is how it explains the prenatal onset of the GATB and QRSL1 families against the infantile onset of the GATC ones. If that model is right, a GATC allele at a more conserved residue should produce a more severe, possibly prenatally lethal, disease, and a milder allele should produce something that survives infancy and has never been recognised as COXPD42. Neither has been reported. Nothing in the current literature can distinguish "COXPD42 is uniformly lethal in infancy" from "the one known GATC allele is lethal in infancy".

steps/7.description: Activating variants in GCK, the beta-cell glucose sensor, raise glucokinase catalytic efficiency and lower its glucose half-saturation concentration. Because glucokinase sets the glucose concentration at which glycolytic flux begins to raise the beta-cell ATP/ADP ratio, the whole secretory system is recalibrated downwards: insulin is released at plasma glucose levels that would normally silence it. The channel itself is intact, which is why this arm converges on the same depolarization node rather than replacing it.

evidence.snippet: In pancreatic β-cells, adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-sensitive K+ (KATP) channels are a central regulator of insulin secretion vital for glucose homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the K-ATP channel as the central regulator of insulin secretion whose defect causes CHI.

evidence.snippet: Genetic defects that lead to loss of expression or function of KATP channels are the most common cause of HI (KATP-HI).
evidence.explanation: Confirms loss of K-ATP channel expression/function as the leading molecular cause of CHI.

steps/8.description: Inactivating variants in ABCC8 (SUR1) or KCNJ11 (Kir6.2), which together form the beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium (K-ATP) channel, cause loss of channel expression or function. The K-ATP channel is the central regulator of insulin secretion: under normal conditions it keeps the beta-cell membrane hyperpolarized when glucose is low. Loss of K-ATP channel function removes this brake on the membrane potential. K-ATP channel defects are the most common molecular cause of CHI and underlie both diffuse and focal histological disease.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in GLUD1 and HADH lead to leucine-induced HH, and these two genes encode the key enzymes glutamate dehydrogenase and short chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase which play a key role in amino acid and fatty acid regulation of insulin secretion respectively.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the GLUD1/HADH amino-acid-driven mechanism as a distinct cause of leucine-induced hyperinsulinism.

evidence.snippet: amino acids can trigger release of insulin in response to the oxidation of amino acids through glutamate via GDH into the TCA cycle under allosteric activation of GDH by leucine.
evidence.explanation: Describes how leucine-activated GDH converges on insulin secretion in the beta cell.

steps/9.description: In a distinct mechanistic arm, dominant activating GLUD1 variants (hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome) or recessive HADH/SCHAD deficiency increase glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH) activity in the beta cell. Leucine allosterically activates GDH, driving glutamate oxidation through the TCA cycle, raising the ATP/ADP ratio, and converging on the same K-ATP-channel closure and insulin-release pathway, producing protein/leucine-sensitive hypoglycemia. Increased GDH activity in liver/kidney also generates the mild hyperammonemia characteristic of HI/HA syndrome.

evidence.snippet: These studies show that promoter-activating mutations in EIHI induce SLC16A1 expression in beta cells, where this gene is not usually transcribed, permitting pyruvate uptake and pyruvate-stimulated insulin release despite ensuing hypoglycemia.
evidence.explanation: Promoter-reporter and expression work in beta cells establishes the ectopic MCT1 expression, the resulting pyruvate uptake, and the pyruvate-stimulated insulin release this node asserts.

steps/10.description: Monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by SLC16A1) is normally silenced in the beta cell, which is what keeps circulating pyruvate and lactate from acting as insulin secretagogues. Promoter variants that de-repress SLC16A1 transcription in the beta cell let pyruvate enter, be oxidized, and stimulate insulin release. Because the trigger is an exogenous monocarboxylate rather than glucose, hypoglycemia appears after anaerobic exercise or a pyruvate load rather than on fasting.

evidence.snippet: Congenital hyperinsulinism (CHI) is a complex heterogeneous condition in which insulin secretion from pancreatic β-cells is unregulated and inappropriate for the level of blood glucose.

steps/12.description: The downstream consequence of K-ATP channel loss of function (or of amino-acid/metabolic defects upstream of the channel) is constitutive beta-cell membrane depolarization, opening of voltage-gated calcium channels, increased cytosolic calcium, and exocytosis of insulin granules. The result is inappropriate insulin secretion that continues despite hypoglycemia, the biochemical hallmark of CHI.

Recurrent or prolonged hypoglycemia carries a considerable risk of seizures, developmental delay, and permanent neurological damage.

steps/3.description: In low-oxygen-affinity variants (Hb F-Toms River, Ggamma67(E11) Val->Met; Hb F-SickKids, Ggamma102(G4) Asn->Ser) the substituted residue lowers both the affinity and the rate of oxygen binding to the mutant subunit. In Hb F-Toms River the larger E11 methionine fills the back of the ligand-binding pocket and sterically impairs oxygen capture; the rate of oxygen release is little changed, so the variant HbF takes up oxygen far more slowly in the lungs and placenta and carries less bound oxygen at physiological pressures. Hb F-SickKids substitutes at the Ggamma102(G4) alpha1-beta2 interface position rather than in the ligand-binding pocket.

open_questions/0.rationale: Recombinant work on this substitution (PMID:29439465) has removed several candidate explanations rather than supplying one. The mutant chain folds correctly, keeps trypsin resistance, moves from ER to Golgi normally, and provokes neither XBP-1 splicing nor caspase-3 activation, so intracellular retention, ER stress and chondrocyte apoptosis are not the route here. The authors conclude the allele "might cause a disease predominantly via extracellular interference". A 2.5 degree Celsius fall in melting temperature is the only measured abnormality, and it is slight. What is still missing is any observation from patient cartilage: fibril architecture, cross-linking, matrix composition, or how a molecule that behaves nearly normally in a recombinant system produces a severe early arthropathy. The tissue selectivity is equally unexplained — the eye and palate are type II collagen tissues and are spared by this allele while other COL2A1 alleles affect them. Both facts are why the fibril node keeps `mechanism_confidence: HYPOTHETICAL` and an INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES edge.

steps/35.description: The single-gene route into the shared cascade. Where type 1 diabetes reaches hyperglycaemia through autoimmune beta-cell destruction and type 2 through insulin resistance with secretory failure, the monogenic forms reach it through a primary functional defect of the beta cell itself: loss of a transcription factor governing pancreatic development and beta-cell function (HNF1A, HNF4A, HNF1B, PDX1, and on current evidence NEUROD1 and RFX6), a raised glucose set point for insulin release (GCK), a mishandled ATP-sensitive potassium channel (ABCC8, KCNJ11), an insulin-gene defect (INS), outright failure of the pancreas to form (PTF1A), or beta-cell loss within a wider syndrome (EIF2AK3, EIF2B1, GLIS3, WFS1, ALMS1, CISD2, SLC19A2, CEL). This node exists so that those genes reach the pathograph; the per-gene mechanisms are not elaborated here, in keeping with the A2 refactor that moved subtype mechanism out of this umbrella entry.

steps/36.description: Sustained hyperglycemia is the shared, subtype-independent driver of diabetic tissue injury across every form of diabetes mellitus. Whatever the upstream route (autoimmune beta-cell destruction in type 1, insulin resistance with beta-cell secretory failure in type 2, undernutrition-associated beta-cell impairment in type 5, or a monogenic beta-cell defect), chronic hyperglycemia feeds one conserved cascade: hyperglycemia-induced oxidative and AGE-RAGE stress, endothelial dysfunction and vascular inflammation, micro- and macrovascular injury, and diabetic end-organ complications (kidney disease, retinopathy, neuropathy, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease). That cascade is captured once in the diabetic_vascular_complications module, to which this node conforms; the per-type entries elaborate their own routes to hyperglycemia.

evidence.snippet: The DIDM is considered to be reversible after discontinuation of diabetogenic treatment, but there is a risk of persistence, which is related to the duration of treatment, prescribed medication, and body mass index.
evidence.explanation: Records that the drug-induced form is considered reversible on stopping the treatment, with a persistence risk related to duration, agent and body mass index. Reversal on withdrawal, bounded by the authors themselves.

edges/29.description: The clearest causal exposure in this entry, because the drug produces the disease rather than raising the chance of it, and because stopping the drug often reverses it. That reversibility is the strongest causal design available anywhere in this entry, and the second item carries it along with its own limit, that persistence depends on treatment duration, agent and body mass.

evidence.snippet: The clinical manifestations of immune checkpoint inhibitor induced diabetes mellitus are variable, and in this case the patient presented with unique primary symptoms.
evidence.explanation: Case report noting that the clinical manifestations of checkpoint-inhibitor-induced diabetes are variable. One patient, and a statement about variability rather than about risk.

edges/30.description: A specific instance of diabetogenic pharmacotherapy that earns its own edge because the mechanism differs: checkpoint blockade releases the brakes on self-reactive T cells and the result is insulin deficiency, sometimes presenting abruptly in ketoacidosis, rather than the insulin resistance most diabetogenic drugs produce. Graded partial because the only evidence is a single case report.

evidence.snippet: Various exogenous triggers, such as certain dietary factors and viruses, are thought to induce the autoimmune process leading in some individuals to extensive beta-cell destruction and ultimately to the clinical manifestation of type 1 diabetes.
evidence.explanation: The same sentence, which names viruses among the exogenous triggers thought to induce the autoimmune process.

edges/31.description: Graded identically to the general islet-autoimmunity exposure and to the early-dietary one, because all three rest on the same sentence of the same paper, which names dietary factors and viruses together. None can be placed above the others on evidence held here.

evidence.snippet: Various exogenous triggers, such as certain dietary factors and viruses, are thought to induce the autoimmune process leading in some individuals to extensive beta-cell destruction and ultimately to the clinical manifestation of type 1 diabetes.
evidence.explanation: The same sentence, which names certain dietary factors among the exogenous triggers thought to induce the autoimmune process. It does not distinguish early from later dietary exposure.

edges/32.description: Recorded as modulating rather than predisposing, which separates it from the viral link despite their sharing a sentence. The exposure's own description and effect field both frame early feeding as modulating the risk of islet autoimmunity in susceptible populations rather than initiating it, and the randomized evidence on infant feeding curated in Type_I_Diabetes is negative.

evidence.snippet: Type II DM remains the most prevalent subtype, as it is closely related to metabolic syndrome, whose prevalence is also rising with a sedentary lifestyle and with consumption of energy-dense, highly processed foods
evidence.explanation: Notes that type 2 diabetes is closely related to metabolic syndrome, whose prevalence is rising with a sedentary lifestyle and Western diet. A statement about co-rising prevalence.

edges/33.description: Traverses the same adiposity to insulin-resistance route as the high-calorie link and so takes the same link type, even though its own sentence names no intermediate: the schema asks whether the field knows the intervening steps, not whether the quoted sentence recites them. The thinness of the evidence is carried by the partial grade on the item instead, which places sedentary lifestyle in the epidemiology of metabolic syndrome rather than following it to insulin resistance.

evidence.snippet: This concept may be clinically valuable, suggesting that hyperinsulinemia associated with excess caloric intake may drive the metabolic dysfunction associated with insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Suggests that hyperinsulinemia associated with excess caloric intake may drive the metabolic dysfunction of insulin resistance. A concept the authors put forward as clinically valuable. The proposed intermediate is hyperinsulinemia/insulin resistance; the sentence does not measure the complete route to chronic hyperglycemia.

edges/34.description: Excess caloric intake may promote hyperinsulinemia and insulin resistance, predisposing to chronic hyperglycemia through this metabolic route.

evidence.snippet: Progression of insulin resistance can lead to metabolic syndrome, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and type 2 diabetes. Insulin resistance is primarily an acquired condition related to excess body fat
evidence.explanation: Names the intervening steps this link relies on and asserts their direction: excess body fat is the primary acquired cause of insulin resistance, and insulin resistance progresses to type 2 diabetes. It is what makes the route rather than the association the content of this edge.

evidence.snippet: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity.
evidence.explanation: A task force recommendation to screen adults aged 35 to 70 with overweight or obesity. A screening rule, which implies risk without stating a mechanism or a magnitude.

edges/35.description: The broadest of the three adiposity exposures and originally the thinnest-evidenced, resting on a screening recommendation alone. The route is the same well-mapped one the other two take, so the link type follows what the field knows rather than what any one sentence states. That recommendation alone would have left the edge asserting a mechanism no cited sentence described, so a second item was added that does describe it, naming excess body fat as the acquired cause of insulin resistance and insulin resistance as a route to type 2 diabetes.

evidence.explanation: This supports ALMS1 as a causative gene in syndromic monogenic diabetes.

evidence.explanation: This supports CISD2 as a causative gene in a monogenic diabetes syndrome.

evidence.explanation: This supports SLC19A2 as a causative gene in a syndromic monogenic diabetes form.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, variants in NEUROD1 and PDX1 were enriched, albeit at levels comparable to RFX6.
evidence.explanation: The burden result that moved PDX1 from insufficient evidence to a supported, low-penetrance MODY gene.

evidence.snippet: The homeodomain protein insulin promoter factor 1 (IPF1) gene, also known as pancreatic duodenal homeobox factor 1 (PDX1), encodes a key transcription that critically regulates early pancreatic development and multiple aspects of beta cell differentiation, maturation, and function.
evidence.explanation: States the beta-cell developmental role that connects PDX1 to the monogenic beta-cell dysfunction node.

genes/20.notes: PDX1 encodes the homeodomain transcription factor that drives pancreatic development and beta-cell differentiation and directly regulates the insulin gene. Biallelic loss causes pancreatic agenesis; heterozygous variants are a rare cause of MODY. ClinGen had flagged PDX1 as a MODY gene whose evidence was insufficient to support or refute; a 2025 case-control burden analysis then found rare damaging PDX1 variants enriched in MODY cases, at a level comparable to the low-penetrance gene RFX6, so the relationship is curated here as causative with low penetrance rather than as disputed.

evidence.snippet: In summary, rare heterozygous variants in NEUROD1 and PDX1 are low-penetrance causes of MODY, while those in APPL1 and WFS1 lack robust genetic evidence for causality and should not be included in MODY testing panels.
evidence.explanation: The study's own summary statement classifying NEUROD1 as a low-penetrance MODY cause.

evidence.snippet: PDX1 and NEUROD1 should be included in MODY gene panels, while heterozygous APPL1 and WFS1 variants should not be reported as causes of MODY.
evidence.explanation: The clinical-testing recommendation that follows from the burden result.

genes/21.notes: NEUROD1 was, like PDX1, on ClinGen's list of MODY genes needing further evidence, and the same 2025 case-control burden analysis found rare damaging variants enriched in MODY cases; both genes are recommended for MODY panels on that basis, with the caveat that penetrance is low.

evidence.snippet: CEL-MODY is a very rare disease caused by frameshift mutations affecting the proximal VNTR segments of the CEL gene.
evidence.explanation: Names the causal allele class for this gene-disease relationship.

evidence.snippet: In total, 21 individuals reported in previous studies were diagnosed with CEL-MODY based on the combination of diabetes and pancreatic exocrine dysfunction as well as frameshift mutations in exon 11 of the CEL gene.
evidence.explanation: Gives the size of the reported literature on this subtype, which is why it is curated as real but very rare.

evidence.snippet: No carriers of CEL missense mutations were reported with exocrine pancreatic dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Supports restricting the causal claim to frameshift VNTR alleles rather than to CEL variants generally.

genes/22.notes: CEL encodes carboxyl ester lipase, an acinar digestive enzyme, making CEL-MODY the one MODY form whose primary lesion is exocrine rather than endocrine: frameshift variants in the proximal segments of the gene's variable-number tandem repeat produce a proteotoxic protein, exocrine pancreatic disease, and only later insulin-dependent diabetes. The allele class matters for diagnosis: the reported cases all carry frameshift variants, and no carrier of a CEL missense variant has been reported with exocrine pancreatic dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in KCNJ11, ABCC8, and INS most commonly cause neonatal diabetes but can be rare causes of MODY.
evidence.explanation: Places INS as a rare MODY gene whose usual presentation is neonatal diabetes.

evidence.snippet: A novel finding was the significant enrichment of only NMD-escape LOF variants in INS (OR=181, p<10-5).
evidence.explanation: Case-control enrichment evidence for INS as a MODY gene, restricted to the NMD-escape allele class.

evidence.snippet: These variants co-segregated with diabetes (logarithm of the odds score=3), included one de novo case, and were absent from >800,000 population control individuals.
evidence.explanation: Cosegregation and population-frequency evidence supporting the INS-MODY relationship.

genes/23.notes: This record is the monogenic insulin-gene claim and is separate from the INS record above, which is the type 1 diabetes INS-region susceptibility association; the two are different assertions about the same gene. Heterozygous INS variants most often cause neonatal diabetes, but missense alleles cosegregating with a MODY phenotype have been reported in several families, and a 2026 burden analysis found loss-of-function alleles that escape nonsense-mediated decay strongly enriched in MODY cases. Deliberately not bound as a gene descriptor on the Monogenic Beta-Cell Dysfunction node: the pathograph keys gene edges on the gene symbol, so doing so would also draw an edge from the type 1 susceptibility record, which makes a different mechanistic claim.

evidence.snippet: Our study demonstrates that heterozygous RFX6 protein truncating variants are associated with MODY with reduced penetrance.
evidence.explanation: The discovery study's own conclusion establishing RFX6 as a reduced-penetrance MODY gene.

evidence.snippet: The hyperglycaemia results from beta-cell dysfunction and is associated with lower fasting and stimulated gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) levels.
evidence.explanation: States the beta-cell mechanism that places RFX6 on the monogenic beta-cell dysfunction node, and the GIP finding that distinguishes it.

genes/24.notes: RFX6 is not in MONDO's causal-gene set for any of the numbered MODY types, and is curated here because the primary literature supports it. Heterozygous protein-truncating RFX6 variants are enriched in MODY cohorts with a large effect size and replicate in independent cohorts, but penetrance is well below that of HNF1A and HNF4A. RFX6 diabetes is also distinguished physiologically by lower fasting and stimulated gastric inhibitory polypeptide levels, which is not a feature of the other MODY forms.

KLF11 was identified on biological candidacy before population reference data existed. ClinGen has reclassified the relationship as refuted.

The same analysis supported PDX1 and NEUROD1, which is why those two are curated here as causative and APPL1 is not.

evidence.snippet: These missense and frameshift mutations mapped to evolutionarily conserved domains adjacent to the catalytic ATPase pocket within SUR2A.
evidence.explanation: States the allele class and the domain, which is what defines this node.

evidence.snippet: One is a frameshift mutation (c.4570_4572delinsAAAT, p.(Leu1524fs)) and the second one is a missense mutation (c.4537G>A, p.(Ala1513Thr)), both altering KATP channel function in vitro and suggesting a mechanistic link to DCM pathogenesis
evidence.explanation: Gives the coding and protein-level descriptions of both founding alleles as restated by a later review.

steps/0.description: A heterozygous exon-38 ABCC9 variant in conserved C-terminal sequence adjacent to the second catalytic ATPase pocket of SUR2A. The two founding alleles are a missense p.(Ala1513Thr) and a frameshift p.(Leu1524fs); neither is a simple whole-protein null, and the frameshift truncates within the nucleotide-binding region rather than removing the subunit. Their location is the mechanistic point - these residues sit where the receptor performs nucleotide catalysis, not where it conducts potassium.

evidence.snippet: Mutant SUR2A proteins showed aberrant redistribution of conformations in the intrinsic ATP hydrolytic cycle, translating into abnormal K(ATP) channel phenotypes with compromised metabolic signal decoding.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the hydrolytic-cycle abnormality as a measured property of the mutant proteins.

steps/1.description: SUR2A is an ABC protein and its nucleotide-binding domains hydrolyse ATP as part of normal channel operation; the hydrolytic cycle is the transduction step, not a housekeeping side reaction. In the mutant receptor the distribution of conformational states across that cycle is shifted, so the receptor no longer reports the prevailing Mg-nucleotide state faithfully to the pore. The defect is qualitative - regulation is displaced rather than simply reduced - which is why the modifier here is DYSREGULATED and not DECREASED.

evidence.snippet: The major ventricular cardiomyocyte KATP channel is composed of SUR2 and Kir6.2, encoded by ABCC9 and KCNJ11, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the subunit composition of the channel whose gating this node describes, and so which cardiac channel an ABCC9 variant acts on.

evidence.snippet: ABCC9 gives rise to distinct SUR2A and SUR2B subunits that differ in the carboxyl terminal 42 amino acids.
evidence.explanation: Explains why a C-terminal ABCC9 variant is isoform-relevant, since the cardiac SUR2A and vascular SUR2B forms differ precisely in that region.

steps/2.description: The sarcolemmal KATP channel is an octamer of four SUR2A subunits around four Kir6.2 pores. With catalysis in SUR2A displaced, the pore's nucleotide sensitivity is set incorrectly: the channel is present and can conduct, but it is no longer under proper regulatory control by the cell's energetic state. That qualitative loss of regulatory control - rather than a quantitative drop in potassium current - is the reason this node carries LOSS_OF_FUNCTION rather than DECREASED.

evidence.snippet: KATP channels are metabolism-gated biosensors functioning as molecular rheostats that adjust membrane potential-dependent functions to match cellular energetic demands.
evidence.explanation: Defines the normal decoding function whose failure this node describes.

evidence.snippet: Ubiquitously expressed throughout the body, ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels couple cellular metabolism to electrical activity in multiple tissues
evidence.explanation: Independent statement of the metabolism-to-electrical-activity coupling this node claims is broken.

steps/3.description: In an intact ventricular cardiomyocyte the KATP channel behaves as a rheostat that couples the ATP/ADP ratio to membrane potential. When the receptor mis-reads that ratio, the coupling between energetic state and electrical behaviour is broken - the cell can no longer translate a metabolic signal into the appropriate change in potassium conductance and membrane potential.

evidence.snippet: K(ATP) channels have been further implicated in the adaptive cardiac response to chronic (patho)physiologic hemodynamic load, with K(ATP) channel deficiency affecting structural remodeling, rendering the heart vulnerable to calcium-dependent maladaptation and predisposing to heart failure.
evidence.explanation: States the adaptive role under chronic load whose failure defines this node, and names the calcium-dependent maladaptation that follows it.

evidence.snippet: The intact KCNJ11-encoded K(ATP) channel is thus a required safety element preventing hypertension-induced heart failure
evidence.explanation: Frames the channel as a stress-conditional safety element, supporting this node through the pore subunit rather than the regulatory subunit.

steps/4.description: This is the primary myocyte insult of CMD1O, and it is conditional rather than constitutive: at rest the heart is largely unremarkable, and the deficit emerges when adrenergic, ischemic, exercise or pressure load raises energetic demand and the myocyte cannot shorten its action potential and trim its membrane-potential-dependent work accordingly. The direct human demonstration is missing; the step is supported by KATP-deficient animals, in which baseline phenotypes are mild and the failure is unmasked by imposed stress.

evidence.snippet: Rescue of the failing K(ATP) knockout phenotype was achieved by alternative control of myocardial calcium influx, bypassing uncoupled metabolic-electrical integration.
evidence.explanation: The rescue experiment that establishes calcium influx as the operative intermediate rather than an epiphenomenon, in the pore-subunit knockout.

evidence.snippet: In the mouse, genetic deletion of Kir6.2 leads to calcium overload and myocardial damage
evidence.explanation: Independent restatement that removing the channel produces calcium overload and myocyte damage, again via the pore subunit.

steps/5.description: Loss of the KATP-dependent brake on membrane-potential-dependent calcium entry permits pathological calcium accumulation in the stressed myocyte. That this is the operative intermediate, and not merely a correlate, is shown by rescue: in the Kir6.2-null mouse the failing phenotype was corrected by controlling myocardial calcium influx by an alternative route, bypassing the uncoupled metabolic-electrical step entirely.

evidence.snippet: Defective decoding of hypertension-induced metabolic distress signals in the K(ATP) channel knockout set in motion pathological calcium overload and aggravated cardiac remodeling through a calcium/calcineurin-dependent cyclosporine-sensitive pathway.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the calcineurin-dependent, cyclosporine-sensitive remodeling pathway that this node names, in the KATP pore knockout.

steps/6.description: Sustained calcium loading activates the calcineurin-NFAT axis and drives a hypertrophic and profibrotic transcriptional programme, converting a reversible signalling failure into structural change. In the KATP knockout this arm is cyclosporine-sensitive, which is what identifies calcineurin as the mediator rather than a bystander.

genes/0.notes: Curated as DISPUTED rather than CAUSATIVE. The ClinGen Dilated Cardiomyopathy Gene Curation Expert Panel classified the ABCC9-dilated cardiomyopathy relationship as LIMITED on 2024-11-15 under SOP10, filed against the parent concept MONDO:0005021 rather than against MONDO:0012062. The human evidence has the shape that produces a Limited call: two probands from one 323-patient screen; segregation supported only by an affected father from whom no DNA was available; no independent replication cohort with comparable functional work; and a ClinVar spectrum in which variants of uncertain significance dominate. Later reports have added further ABCC9 alleles in Mexican and Chinese DCM cohorts, which is genuine accumulation but has not yet moved the classification. MONDO nonetheless models CMD1O as a gene-anchored disease concept, which is why this entry exists - DISPUTED records the evidence state, it does not retire the concept.

treatments/2.description: There is no genotype-specific therapy for CMD1O. hypotheses/0.description: The proposed model: a C-terminal ABCC9 variant displaces SUR2A's catalytic cycle, the Kir6.2 pore is consequently mis-gated, the cardiomyocyte cannot match electrical and contractile work to energetic demand under stress, calcium overload follows, and calcineurin-dependent remodeling converts that into a dilated, arrhythmogenic ventricle. The molecular arm is demonstrated in recombinant systems; the myocardial arm is supported by KATP-deficient animals but has never been shown for an ABCC9 catalytic-domain allele in a heart, human or otherwise. It is recorded as EMERGING rather than CANONICAL because the gene-disease relationship it explains is itself classified as Limited.
